question: Your team runs a custom slash command in Claude Code that reads benchmark reports from two performance teams and writes a performance section for the project documentation. Both reports are credible and were collected in the same week on the same hardware, but they state different p99 latency values for one endpoint. The generated section shows only one value, cites one report, and does not mention the other report. Which instruction in the command file most likely caused this?

options.text: It tells Claude to give one definitive value per metric, so Claude picks one credible figure instead of listing both with sources and annotating the conflict.
options.reason: The guide says to annotate conflicting statistics from credible sources with source attribution. An instruction that demands one value leads Claude to arbitrarily select one figure and lose the other.

options.text: It does not ask for collection dates, so Claude treats a temporal difference between the reports as a contradiction and drops the older value.
options.reason: Both reports were collected in the same week, so time does not explain the different values. This is a real conflict between credible sources, and the guide says to annotate it rather than select one value.

options.text: It asks Claude to present benchmark figures as a table, and a table cannot show two attributed values for the same metric.
options.reason: The guide names tables as a suitable format for some content, such as financial data, and nothing in it limits a table to one value per metric. A table can list both values with their sources, so the format is not the cause.

options.text: It asks Claude to keep a claim-source mapping for each figure, and that mapping allows only one source to support each claim.
options.reason: The guide presents claim-source mappings as the way to preserve attribution through synthesis. A mapping can show both values with their sources, so it does not force one source per claim.
